(1) FinBERT, a pre-trained model, is a good starting point for financial sentiment analysis; (2) the performance of the model can be improved by fine-tuning it on a small dataset; (3) a small amount of data is enough to train a model with high accuracy; (4) the model can be further improved by adding additional data from the same domain
the transfer of language models trained on general domains to a financial domain is effective, and can be improved by adding financial domain-specific knowledge to the model.

(1) pre-trained language models are a powerful tool for domain adaptation in sentiment classification tasks, and (2) FinBERT is a state-of-the-art model for financial sentiment analysis, which can be used for a wide range of tasks in finance.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

FinBERT is a language model that is based on BERT and is able to improve the performance of the state of the art in financial sentiment classification by 14 percentage point for the FinancialPhrasebank dataset.
FinBERT is the state-of-the art language model for financial sentiment analysis.

FinBERT outperforms the state-of-the art models for financial sentiment classification, and the performance gap between general sentiment classification and financial sentiment classification is reduced by transfer learning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transfer of knowledge from a large general-domain corpus to the specific financial domain improves the performance significantly, and the performance can be further boosted by fine-tuning the model on a small amount of labeled data.
we show that pre-trained language models can significantly improve performance on financial sentiment analysis tasks, and we release the pre-trained model for the research community.
FinBERT is the first language model for sentiment analysis in the financial domain and it can be used to improve the performance of existing sentiment classification methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transfer learning is an effective way to improve the performance in niche domains with limited training data.
pre-trained models can be successfully adapted to new domains without the need of labeled data.

pre-trained language models, such as BERT, can be easily adapted to new tasks by fine-tuning the model with domain-specific training data, which is a significant improvement compared to previous work that relied on domain-specific training data to train the models from scratch.
